thread:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT — streaming latency spike detected on us-east-1 cluster (p95 480ms -> 1.8s, p99 1.2s -> 6.9s). Error rates for streaming sessions +15%. Auto-fallbacks triggered: 3 model fallbacks. ECC correctable errors creeping on node gpu-node-17.

oncall-amber: @channel paging oncall. I’m acknowledging, will triage.

oncall-amber: summary? which service?

incident-bot: service: inference-runtime/streaming. affected route: /v1/chat/stream. region: us-east-1. 90th percentile requests routed to gpu-node-17. Recent syslog snippets attached to alert.

mike: I’m on-call and en route. pulling metrics now — checking dashboards.

jess: I’m with runtime, if we need immediate routing changes I can push a temporary policy.

mike: p95 across cluster jumped to ~1.9s for the last 10m; p99 around 7s. Streaming stalls: partial frames, client connections hang for ~10-12s before retry.

sre-alex: logs show repeated ECC correctable on gpu0/gpu1 on gpu-node-17: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1e.0): GPU has fallen off the bus.` — intermittent. Thermal sensors show spikes preceding ECC.

infra-sam: hardware telemetry for node 17: fan duty oscillating 40->100% under load, core temp spikes to 92C for short bursts then cools. This is consistent with thermal throttling.

eng-runtime-lina: If node flaps KV cache, streaming sessions that hit warmed KV will stall. We need to avoid hitting that node. Recommend immediate traffic drainage + model fallback to a lower-memory quantized variant on healthy nodes.

mike: Agreed. Plan: 1) mark gpu-node-17 as `quarantine` in fleet, 2) enable soft-routing to exclude it, 3) scale up warm pools on other nodes and enable 2x burst capacity for streaming for ~10m, 4) set rate-limit throttle for non-critical routes.

jess: I can push the routing change — will add a canary and 30s monitoring window. Pushing now: `./infractl route set --exclude-node gpu-node-17 --policy soft-fallback --region us-east-1`

incident-bot: deploy-bot: routing policy change applied (canary 5% -> 100% over 30s).

mike: Draining node now: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 && ./drain_streaming_node.sh gpu-node-17 --grace 45s`

infra-sam: Quarantine label applied. Node marked `unschedulable`. Jobs draining. Observability: CPU and memory stabilize on draining nodes.

customer-success-amy: any customer-facing impact? I’m on standby for CS updates.

mike: So far a minority of sessions hit the node; autoscaling absorbed most load. We did see degraded tail latency for a handful of enterprise customers (3 support tickets opened, ticket ids: #23478 #23479 #23480). Suggest a short status update: "We detected intermittent GPU hardware errors causing degraded streaming latency; mitigations applied; investigating root cause."

jess: Also toggled model fallback to quantized-2 for streaming route: `policy: prefer_quantized_on_spillover` — this reduced token-latency on warm nodes.

sre-alex: Quick checks: `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` output (excerpt):
```
GPU 0: Correctable ECC errors: 412
GPU 1: Correctable ECC errors: 398
Last corrected timestamp: 2026-05-14T09:12:10Z
```
That rate over last 2 hours is abnormal.

infra-sam: I’m collecting nvml logs and raising a hardware ticket to the vendor. Recommend we isolate the card(s) for replacement during maintenance window.

eng-runtime-lina: Observed stream stall stack traces show KV cache miss -> remote fetch -> long wait when node is flapping. We should add guardrails to avoid routing hot sessions to nodes with recent ECC counts > 100 in 1h.

mike: Good postmortem item. For now mitigation standing: node quarantined, routing changed, model fallback enabled, warm pool scaled. Monitoring shows p95 down to ~420ms and p99 back to ~1.1s after 6m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied. Latency trending downward. Continuing to monitor for 1h.

customer-success-amy: Sending a short note to the affected customers and triaging tickets. Will CC on any escalations.

jess: Can we confirm if any canary fails during full traffic shift? Observability dashboard green at canary completion.

mike: Canary succeeded. Rolling to 100% at +30s completed.

infra-sam: Hardware ticket created: HT-987654. Vendor acknowledged, requested NVML dump and dmesg. I’ve uploaded logs and included `nvidia-smi -q` captures.

sre-alex: Safe follow-up: schedule maintenance to remove node, run memtest/driver reflash, replace GPU if ECC continues after driver.

mike: Customer impact summary for post-incident report: ~0.7% of streaming traffic saw p99 spikes >5s during the incident window (09:06-09:14 UTC). 3 enterprise customers opened tickets; no data loss reported. Mitigations prevented a broader outage.

customer-success-amy: Copying that into the incident summary, will notify customers with the suggested wording.

jess: Action items (short-term):
- infra-sam: escalate hardware ticket and provide ETA for replacement (HT-987654)
- eng-runtime-lina: add a routing gate to exclude nodes with ECC > 100 in 1h
- sre-alex: add a dashboard and alert threshold for thermal excursions (temp > 85C for 3 samples within 5m)
- mike: write immediate incident summary and handoff to morning oncall

mike: I’m handing off to morning oncall @jess for follow-up after 09:30 UTC.

oncall-amber: Acknowledged handoff. Good work team, keep logs in ticket.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigation): status -> stable. Follow-ups scheduled in the incident board.

mike: leaving a short log snippet for the postmortem: `drain start 09:07:31, quarantine label applied 09:07:55, routing shift complete 09:08:40, p99 recovery 09:12:15`

eng-runtime-lina: adding runbook note: consider `soft-fallback` policy by default for streaming until we have better ECC gating.

infra-sam: vendor responded with preliminary hardware diagnostics — suspect aging thermal paste and fan controller jitter. Scheduling on-site check tomorrow 02:00 local.

sre-alex: tagging postmortem owners. Will run root cause triage and include telemetry.

customer-success-amy: I’ve updated customers: "We identified intermittent GPU hardware errors causing transient increases in latency. We have isolated the affected node and taken steps to prevent recurrence. We will follow up with a timeline for hardware remediation."

mike: thanks all. closing thread after we confirm vendor ETA.

oncall-amber: closing ack. :white_check_mark:
